title: A free community catalog for game developers (including vibecoders)
author: BlazeEcho
selftext:
[https://catalog.hearthengine.com/](https://catalog.hearthengine.com/)

You can upload a browser build, or just link out to your itch page, Steam page, or wherever the game already lives (for free ofc). You also have your own profile people can follow/track.

I felt like there wasn't really a fleshed out platform for us to post our \[vibecoded\] games on and get some players so here we are. It's super sparse right now but every new user will build the community, and I want to expand into giving away different resources and tools here in the future. Any feedback would be appreciated.

comments.author: FoundOnExit9Teen
comments.body:
Actually there is a website just like this called

[slagdock.com](http://slagdock.com) , over 100 games all from indie developers from this sub and others

comments.author: cant-game-anymore
comments.body: I was thinking about this literally yesterday. My main question to you is how is this different than itch.io?

replies.author: BlazeEcho
replies.body:
hey! right now i think it's mainly the low user friction as well as the lack of saturation.

a lot of devs here just make simple games they want to post somewhere so rather than going through the whole process with itch they can just upload their files and put in some small details. we also offer ways for agents to upload for you.

and [itch.io](http://itch.io) is filled with tons of incumbents so this is kind of a fresh platform where there's a higher chance someone might stumble upon your game.
